direct_interfaces.checked_use: finite candidate families make the rho maximum and beta minimum attained; the direction is existence of a finite maximum/minimum, never a supremum.
nonempty finite averaging gives a low-degree row and an at-most-average selected subset; neither consumer reverses the average inequality.
the ordinary published blockade has nonempty blocks and positive width; QID deliberately extends only its sequence convention to empty blocks, while a positive-width output is an ordinary blockade.
the QID restriction keeps the published ordered-block sparsity language but makes its empty-tail convention explicit; it does not infer symmetric sparsity.
all uses retain the source direction: later vertices have bounded degree into an earlier block, and a labelled blowup demands both directions only where it explicitly says so.
the homogeneous parameter uses induced-subgraph densities only for sets of size at least two; singleton and null cases are separated before any quotient.
ind_H is the finite labelled-embedding count. The recurrence uses monotone inclusion ind_H(F)<=ind_H(G), not the unrelated strict-inheritance interface.
the density numerator is labelled induced embeddings, preserving adjacency and nonadjacency, rather than unlabelled image sets.
all displayed base-2 logarithms have positive arguments and base different from one; the definition does not license boundary evaluation at x=1/2.

for every real r there is a unique floor(r) with floor(r)<=r<floor(r)+1. This supplies every displayed floor and the two least-natural constructions t=-floor(-u) and m=-floor(-eta gamma_1|F|); no undeclared ceiling convention remains.
direct_interfaces.axiom_strength: the supplier uses Archimedean order and well-ordering of N, not a choice principle.

direct_interfaces.checked_use: the finite m-subset double count uses the exact binomial incidence multiplicities with 0<=m<=|A|; it does not divide by an undefined binomial coefficient.
special-copy fibres are finite labelled-map families, including the empty-domain convention; the count does not replace embeddings by unverified images.
each use sums the same finite incidence relation in two orders: degrees for trimming, subset-edge incidences for selection, and special-copy fibres for the trichotomy.
base-2 length and exponent conversions retain positive bases and arguments; the examples only substitute within the theorem's open domain.
the derivative/integral proof establishes log_2 y<=y for y>=2, which is used only to verify subreciprocity of the logarithmic function.
strict increase and product/quotient laws justify positive logarithmic denominators, monotonicity of ell, and the eventual-ratio comparison; no asymptotic inequality is used outside its stated range.
disjoint labelled block choices multiply, including the empty-extension product; the example's 3^3 and 3^2 are labelled counts.
all bases are positive before exponents are combined, reversed, or rescaled; the proof plans do not apply real-power rules at zero.
the forbidden vertices form a finite subset of the next block, so the lower bound leaves an available vertex and distinct extensions remain injective.
the extension count partitions labelled extensions by their next selected vertex; disjointness, rather than an overlapping union, is the used hypothesis.
the exact binom(n,2) convention controls internal densities, the subset-selection incidence count, and the final km-vertex density inequality, with singleton cases kept separate.

semantic_checks.result: Graphs and all candidate families are finite; ind_H counts labelled induced embeddings; null-pattern and singleton cases are explicitly separated; density is never divided by binom(0,2) or binom(1,2).

The published blockade remains nonempty and positive-width. The local QID sequence alone permits empty blocks, and every sparse relation has its direction recorded; complement use swaps density alternatives, not an unproved closure property of H-free graphs.

Every floor has lem-integer-part in its declared dependency chain. The only former ceiling uses are now t=-floor(-u) and m=-floor(-eta gamma_1|F|), with their one-unit bounds stated before use; all base-2 logarithm arguments and denominators are positive.

The amplification lemma now quantifies ell,H,c,d,h,epsilon,z,b,x,p,eta,t,delta,G and its fixed beta profile. Its <= copy-count hypothesis and delta|G|>1 yield the F-size and divisivity hypotheses in the required direction, and iteration reaches beta_t=1 only after p^t epsilon^2>=1.

The direct proof route is finite combinatorics plus complete ordered-real arithmetic; its floor supplier uses Archimedean order and well-ordering of N, not Choice. No item in the declared closure has a deps, justified_by, or load-bearing forward_refs path to deferred-set-theory-beyond-choice.
